title: Exposure Read across a Profile's Northbeam Credit Accounts
content:
Exposure on the Northbeam Store Credit and Financing Accounts is read across every account the profile holds rather than account by account: the balances carried are set against the sum of the limits.

## The basis

1. The balances carried are the sum of what is owed on every account of the profile standing active, delinquent or suspended, taken as it stands at the moment of handling, with no historical window behind it. That sum is set against the sum of the limits of those accounts.
2. A draw that would take total utilisation past the product's suspension figure is refused even where the single account has room.
3. A limit increase on one account is considered against total exposure and the income stated on the request, and the increase is never written above the product's largest limit.
4. A Northbeam Business Fleet Line of Credit and a Northbeam Business Net Thirty Account are read together, because the same business stands behind both.
5. Store credit held on any account reduces exposure only when it is actually spent, not while it sits unspent.
6. Where the profile also carries a promotional financing plan, the balance on that plan counts toward exposure at its full amount however far off its end day is.

## The basis as inputs, judgement and result

- **Inputs.** Every account of the profile standing active, delinquent or suspended; what is owed on each; the limit of each; any promotional plan balance; the income stated on a limit request where an increase is in question.
- **Judgement.** Total utilisation is what is owed across those accounts against the limits across those accounts, and the product's suspension figure is read against that total, not against the one account.
- **Result.** A draw that would carry the total past that figure is refused; a limit increase is written no higher than the largest limit the product is written to.

## A worked reading on hypothetical figures

A profile holds two accounts of the range, one with a limit of 1000.00 and one with a limit of 3000.00, so the limits sum to 4000.00 US dollars. The first owes 600.00 and the second owes 2900.00, so the balances carried sum to 3500.00. Total utilisation is therefore 3500.00 against 4000.00, which is 87.5 per cent of the limits taken together, and it is that figure the product's suspension figure is read against — not the 60.0 per cent the first account shows on its own.

If one of those accounts also holds 200.00 of unspent store credit, the 3500.00 is unchanged, because store credit reduces exposure only once it is actually spent. If 500.00 of the 2900.00 sits on a promotional financing plan, that 500.00 still counts in the 3500.00 at its full amount, whatever its end day.

All the amounts in this reading are hypothetical inputs chosen to work the basis through; none of them is a figure any product in the range sets.
